SWARM-01.blocker: Normal Auto/Manual × Swarm launch paths and an opt-in UI are not wired; fixture planning cannot verify off-mode or one-agent fallback.

SWARM-02.blocker: Saved allowlists are snapshotted, but live target discovery and permission-aware fallback or checkpoint transfer are absent.

SWARM-03.blocker: Exact planned resource claims survive restart, constrain parallel benefit and cannot be omitted or downgraded at admission. Full chain/independent replay, real worktree writer isolation and undeclared-resource discovery remain incomplete.

SWARM-04.blocker: Read-only target preview is deterministic and provider-label agnostic; actual scheduling, reservations and replay are not implemented.

SWARM-05.blocker: A fixture-only decision persists cost estimates by revision and batch, gates second-worker admission, and now refills a completed slot while other workers stay active. Planned exact-name write conflicts force serial choice. Supervised worker wall time is measured, but actual native usage and phase costs, undeclared-resource independence, live calibrated estimates and shared Auto Mode quota input remain absent.

SWARM-06.blocker: Capability requirements reject a cheaper unqualified target in fixtures; real quality routing and launch gating are not implemented.

SWARM-07.blocker: Fixture Swarm and ordinary launches share the global slot check in both directions; lower-maximum draining, reviewer/native-descendant control and live activation remain unimplemented.

SWARM-08.blocker: Fixture swarm admissions and ordinary task.create serialize global slots, including concurrent ordinary launches after Swarm admission; ordinary tasks still lack shared account-quota reservations and live Auto Mode pool identity.

SWARM-09.blocker: Fixture targets sharing a pool share reservations across categories, and targets labeled as one account with no common pool now fail closed; live account identity discovery and proof of independent accounts remain unavailable.

SWARM-10.blocker: Fixture allocation freezes at first admission and preserves a finishing reserve. Confirmed exit moves a reservation to uncertain while continuing to bind capacity; authoritative actual usage reconciliation and finishing-work draw are not implemented.

SWARM-11.blocker: Each fixture quota window is reserved separately, and a new window ID no longer grants an ongoing run a second allocation or forgets prior attempts in the same pool/unit. Live reset detection, native usage reconciliation, unlike-unit end-to-end admission and a full short/long-window run remain unverified.

SWARM-12.blocker: Unknown, stale and estimated quota get explicit preview reasons; live telemetry, permission revocation and actual admission are not implemented.

SWARM-13.blocker: Live adapter enforcement and native usage reconciliation are absent; quota evidence remains injected fixture data.

SWARM-14.blocker: Fixture outage/auth failures exclude only affected targets; rate limits, real adapters and running-job response are not implemented.

SWARM-15.blocker: Two fixture target routes now transition a failed supervised launch from ready to failed after the second attempt, retain the cap across revision, and block retry when an effect is unknown. Live routing and unchanged-state model-planning suppression remain unverified.

SWARM-16.blocker: No live worker checkpoint transfer or external side-effect reconciliation exists; artifact persistence alone is insufficient.

SWARM-17.blocker: Native descendant admission/control or disablement has not been qualified per harness; observed children are not enforced limits.

SWARM-18.blocker: A versioned S3 fixture integrates 26 contract/module commits in an isolated worktree and preserves its source checkout. Unsaved buffers, service-side writes, live worker isolation and normal launch-path enforcement remain unverified.

SWARM-19.blocker: The versioned S3 fixture integrates a repaired contract and 24 module patches; a combined check fails after four and passes at the final commit. A local daemon-crash replay now holds an orphaned checker until exit and requires a fresh check. Live sandboxed verification, termination of a permanently hung orphan, director conflict resolution and normal adapter integration remain unqualified.

SWARM-20.blocker: Stop interrupts linked scripted local workers, blocks pending launch replay, and retries a simulated failed first signal after daemon restart. A fresh run readout exposes unconfirmed linked workers until confirmed exit. Live Pause checkpoints, native descendants, reservation/exit display in VS Code, and full off-mode drain remain unverified.

SWARM-21.blocker: Revision CAS, affected-job invalidation and stale result rejection pass; user-message intake, live delivery, and job removal remain unimplemented.

SWARM-22.blocker: Fixture startup automatically drains already-admitted unlinked intents only while their snapshots and target permission remain valid; it retains stale or revoked reservations without launching. Exact spawn-record crash windows, result receipt replay, VS Code restart, live Auto Mode refresh and live harness recovery remain unverified.

SWARM-23.blocker: The extension has no Swarm status/usage/limiting-constraint view; daemon fixture output is not UI evidence.

SWARM-24.blocker: The fixture admission revalidates a target snapshot transactionally and ordinary launches share the global slot lock; the actual Auto Mode producer and shared account-quota authority are not integrated.

SWARM-25.blocker: No authorized version-pinned live two-worker, fallback, cancel and recovery matrix has been run.

SWARM-26.blocker: No fixed end-to-end serial-versus-swarm evaluation suite or native usage/elapsed-time comparison exists.

SWARM-27.blocker: Supervised scripted workers submit evidence/results into the director inbox, accepted contract work unlocks a dependent job, and fixture completion requires passed checks for every accepted job plus confirmed exits and an applied inbox. A live director still cannot decompose, route, review or synthesize the objective.

SWARM-28.blocker: Policy previews qualified targets, but no live Auto Mode route and worker launch connects capability decisions to jobs.

SWARM-29.blocker: A deterministic 100-job fixture admits 32 attempts at a time and accepts all 100 exactly once with intact synthetic evidence; a separate fixture runs 32 supervised local processes alongside a scripted active director turn, and quota headroom reduces effective concurrency with a reason. A working model director, executed checks and combined 100-job supervised/provider path remain unverified.

SWARM-30.blocker: A fixture stalls on unknown director termination, preserves worker reservation/result and prior Pause state, and requeues an unapplied batch after confirmed replacement with generation fencing; live process liveness, replacement availability and actual director execution are unverified.

SWARM-31.blocker: A scripted local launch remains separate from completion, replays to one run, and emits a once-only terminal event automatically without accepting the job; native async receipts, silent/stale output, late append, descendants and usage reconciliation remain unverified.

SWARM-32.blocker: Fixture admission holds at eight submitted results and resumes below four with bounded waves; outage recovery and actual director review capacity remain unimplemented.

SWARM-33.blocker: A fixture batch claims at most 20 messages/32 KiB and Stop halts future claims; no model turn, reservation, or semantic review runs.

SWARM-34.blocker: A 100-job fixture proves bounded director pages, a bounded worker brief attached to scripted launch, same-target accepted-dependency references, and chunked retrieval. Live harness delivery, destination-specific context grants/revocation, token accounting, complete scope/resource/budget briefs, and on-demand director mediation remain unverified.

SWARM-35.blocker: S3 contract repair uses attempt 2 of the same logical job, redirects one stale module result and integrates 24 module patches. Applied revision acknowledgement, director conflict resolution, qualified session reuse and the complete S3 workflow remain unverified.

SWARM-36.blocker: A fixture-only central queue fairly admits a 100-job and two-job backlog through one durable admission transaction. It does not yet start directors/workers automatically, route per-job targets through Auto Mode, reserve an actual director process, or prove cross-category scope and handoff isolation in a live run.

SWARM-37.blocker: No 100-job/32-worker Swarm UI fixture, aggregate view or measured Pause/Stop acknowledgement latency exists.

SWARM-38.blocker: Pinned behavior and intentional reuse differences are documented, but Auto Mode usage/discovery and Swarm director recovery/native-child ordering gaps remain unverified.

SWARM-39.blocker: Built-in defaults, saved precedence, approved-target inheritance, immutable run snapshots and percentage override arithmetic pass; actual S0 launch, one-time selection UI, immediate revocation and full scheduler enforcement remain unimplemented.

SWARM-40.blocker: The fixture allocation freezes 10% of available native units, preserves at least 20% for finishing, and rejects zero estimates; all cost classes and live shared accounting remain incomplete.

SWARM-41.blocker: The joined S1 replay deduplicates D1, claims it before J2 finishes, and records targeted J1/J4 advisory receipts; the guarded J7 fault replay records scripted retractions with receipts. A separate supervised scripted worker applies broker messages. Live harness delivery, semantic recipient choice and actual director inference remain unimplemented.

SWARM-42.blocker: Stable-ID dedupe, terminal exact-receipt replay after restart, stale generation checks and late finished-attempt result isolation pass; the joined S1 replay includes duplicate D1. Live dispatch/accounting and broader delayed/reordered message traces remain untested.

SWARM-43.blocker: The joined S1 replay records delivered/applied advisories and J4 overlap redirect; a separate supervised scripted worker acknowledges a targeted advisory. The specified revision-2 assignment, redirect during a long tool call, the 30-second applied-ack timeout and qualified live delivery remain unimplemented.

SWARM-44.blocker: Cross-category read/write claims and duplicate hypothesis ownership pass; joined S1 records J4 overlap and scripted redirect while J1 separately checks project middleware. Director redirection is not connected to live workers.

SWARM-45.blocker: Joined S1 adds J7 after J2's task result and independently reproduces it from a fresh PostgreSQL schema within the worker ceiling. Director-selected budgeted creation, contradiction handling and finding merge remain unimplemented.

SWARM-46.blocker: The S3 fixture redirects one in-flight revision-1 module and rejects its stale result after contract repair. An S1 fault replay rejects stale J4 evidence and sends a scripted retraction to J2/J4 after contradictory J7 evidence. Applied acknowledgement across qualified live sessions, autonomous correction, and unrelated accepted-work preservation in this scenario remain unverified.

SWARM-47.blocker: A later contradictory result invalidates the prior review and prevents final completion, but S1 cross-worker contradictions, independent reproduction, explicit unresolved synthesis and live director review remain unimplemented.

SWARM-48.blocker: Fixture plan validation, independent subgraphs, two failed plan/repair validation turns, recorded accepted-evidence progress, and durable two-turn no-progress stalls pass. Other material-progress and repair-error classes, live director behavior, and complete S3/S5 traces remain unverified.

SWARM-49.blocker: Malformed or unauthorized worker reports get bounded non-leaking diagnostics and no inbox effect; payload/inbox bounds, dedupe of 2,000 local-socket replays, Stop under two seconds during that flood, bounded director batches, admission hold at a full inbox, and terminal report persistence pass in fixtures. Live inference/context controls and broader permission paths remain unverified.

SWARM-50.blocker: Injected SQLite failures during result state update and reservation insertion roll back atomically; live launch intent, disk-full recovery, and persisted blocked-state UX remain unimplemented.

SWARM-51.blocker: Local supervised fixtures now distinguish output silence, interrupted transport, disconnected/unconfirmed exit, prompt suspect retry, progress spam, crash between job-timeout persistence and interrupt, and a worker ignoring the first signal. Confirmed exit keeps the reservation binding as uncertain. A 60-second wall-clock outage, late launch/review race, worker ignoring all escalation, shared usage settlement, and qualified live harness behavior remain unverified.

SWARM-52.blocker: The fixture integration API now defaults runs to no source-change permission, retains it over restart, and requires an explicit isolated-write grant. Generic workers still have writable worktrees; no qualified audit-only harness sandbox, live-service mutation boundary or S1/S2/S4 replay exists.

SWARM-53.blocker: Fixture admission atomically acquires durable planned claims even when the request omits them, rejects claim downgrades, and holds conflicting read/write requests until release; real tool/resource discovery, contamination detection and selective rerun remain unimplemented.

SWARM-54.blocker: Acceptance and fixture final completion revalidate stored evidence provenance and integrity, including tampering after review. Dependent context now excludes unreviewed artifacts and becomes unavailable after a late source result. Live filesystem provenance and permission-scoped replacement retrieval remain unimplemented.

SWARM-55.blocker: Fixture results retain distinct negative, environment-failure and defect states; the versioned S1 backend now proves a missing export queue stays blocked through Swarm coverage and completion. Defect acceptance requires reproduction evidence and later results invalidate prior review. A complete endpoint/permission coverage matrix, S2 backend replay, autonomous director decisions and live harness paths remain unverified.

SWARM-56.blocker: Local fixtures enforce review pressure, preserve ten already-admitted results across the eight-result threshold and daemon restart, and launch 32 live supervised workers with explicit ceilings. Live account usage, director/reviewer operation at scale and versioned qualification remain unverified.

SWARM-57.blocker: Durable fixture destination grants transfer only accepted evidence to an admitted dependent target, survive restart, and yield to revocation. Revocation blocks context delivery and dependent admission, interrupts a linked worker, and retries after daemon crash while an unrelated worker remains active. Scripted Stop/revocation/result/acceptance orderings now pass. Live cross-target ACL/credential isolation, secret audits, peer bypass resistance, S4 replay and simultaneous native races remain unverified.

SWARM-58.blocker: A fixture-only durable intent journal blocks duplicate execution and replacement after a lost acknowledgement, including revision and restart; Stop and revision preserve a conflicting resource claim. Actual tool calls are not intercepted, the external outcome probe is not independently qualified, safe claim release after quarantine is missing, and live S2 reconciliation remains unverified.

SWARM-59.blocker: Fixture observations now persist a specific availability block, hold admission and idle director turns, preserve active worker evidence, and wake once when eligibility or finishing headroom returns within the original deadline. Live Auto Mode updates, a normal status UI, user-triggered target changes and live director behavior remain unverified.

SWARM-60.blocker: Worker discoveries reach a durable director inbox and fixture director advisories reach only selected peers with applied receipts; live peer delivery, automatic relevance selection and artifact permissions are not implemented.

SWARM-61.blocker: Pending local launch replay is rejected after Stop, a linked scripted worker is interrupted, and rejected/superseded work does not requeue after cancellation. A crash fixture persists revocation, retries the dependent-worker interrupt after restart, and leaves an unrelated worker running. Four scripted Stop/revocation/result/acceptance orderings persist a shared sequence, preserve late results, and block new launches. A simulated failed Stop signal is retried after daemon restart. Simultaneous native races, native descendants, qualified live paths, and explicit user resume remain unverified.

SWARM-62.blocker: A daemon timer checks deadlines without admission requests, records a deadline reason, cancels queued work, interrupts a linked scripted worker and delivers its terminal event. A stopping-run readout now exposes unconfirmed workers, proven in a Stop fixture; deadline-specific readout, live checkpoint/interrupt, VS Code display, and explicit extension remain unverified.

SWARM-63.blocker: No ordinary backend Swarm run can launch yet; its absence cannot verify that product self-tests/editor control are excluded.

SWARM-64.blocker: S3 and S1 have versioned backends and joined scripted runs. S1 covers seven isolated database probes, D1/overlap messages, slot refill, J7 reproduction and evidence-gated completion; separate fault replays cover missing artifact, stale J4 output, contradictory J7 with scripted retractions, and unavailable J5 export queue. Autonomous decisions, remaining S1/S3 fault and report traces, live communication and S0/S2/S4/S5 remain unverified.

S0.blocker: No normal category + objective launch control or live director selection exists; policy defaults only have daemon fixture coverage.

S1.blocker: Versioned Express/PostgreSQL probes feed a joined scripted Swarm run with four initial workers, D1/overlap coordination, slot refill, J7 reproduction and seven accepted checks. Separate fault runs reject missing/stale evidence, hold contradictory J7 with scripted retractions, and classify a missing export queue as blocked coverage. Profile/director choices, detailed report, source-text injection, contradiction resolution, and live communication remain open.

S2.blocker: The local evt-42 fixture proves one side-effect application across lost acknowledgement and restart, but the versioned S2 payment fixture, signed webhook, queue barrier, protected variant, independent outcome probe and full director trace are missing.

S3.blocker: One scripted run of the versioned 24-module fixture joins contract repair, stale-result rejection, four-to-eight admission, review backpressure, 26 isolated integration commits and evidence-gated completion. Autonomous director adaptation, a live run, conflict repair, scope narrowing and qualified harness paths remain unverified.

S4.blocker: No versioned Dispatch incident bundle, permission-aware account replacement or live checkpoint handoff exists.

S5.blocker: Individual fault fixtures exist, but the complete ordered Atlas replay and all injected faults have not been executed.
